institutionName: University of Natural Resources and Life Sciences, Vienna (BOKU)

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Career opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The location of Vienna in the middle of Europe is very convenient to do short trips into other countries and get to know other cultures as well. Also the closeness to mountains and forests is very nice and there are a lot of cultural things going on in the city, it is never boring.

questions.answer:
Shared flats are easy to find on WG-gesucht. de and on
willhaben.at
, but it is recommendable to start looking on time, 2 or 3 months in advance.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It would be good to find something close to the university because the city is quite big and it can take some time to get there otherwise. But the public transport system is very good and well connected.

How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration was quite easy as far as I remember. But every single course has its own registration period depending on when it starts. Most of them start in October and therefore the registration period is also in this month but it depends.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: We got E-mails with step by step introductions and also on the webpage of the university all the information can be found (but it can be a bit confusing sometimes).

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It was a bit stressful in the beginning because I wanted to try out different courses and avery course had its own registration periods and criterias, but once I knew which courses I wanted to take everything worked out.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don´t try too many courses because it will take time in which you might have lectures everyday with changing schedules. Be aware that you also have to register for the correspondent exam, it is not done automatically when you register for a course.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 2 semesters

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Ecology of aquatic systems, Rhizosphere processes and application to agriculture and soil protection, Ecological river landscape management, Sustainable land use in developing countries, Plant and environment, Soil ecology, Innovations for sustainable forest management, Mountain forest climatology and headwater hydrology

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
questions.answer: Master´s thesis seminar

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: "Innovations in forest management" because it gave a new perspective on the role of forests in our community and "sustainable land use in developing countries" because it was very different from other courses with many guest lecturers which were talking about their own experience and about many different topics, all very interesting!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Different events on the evening, some Erasmus events, different sport courses but we had to pay for them, dancing evenings on Mondays, flee markets.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Playing beachvolleyball at the Danube because sport always helps to socialize and get to know new people and the Gürtelconnection events where a lot of different regional artists were playing their music in different pubs.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Trips to Budapest, Brno, Bratislava and Salzburg. Daytrip and hiking at Rax. Skiing in the Alps. Biking along the Danube.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was easy because I was only living in shared flats with local people and speaking german helps a lot of course.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Sport and some kind of regular activities is the best way to get in contact with local people.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: In general, people in Vienna are less polite but as far as I remember I had only some view strange encounters with elder people, the young people is in general nice, specially at BOKU because of the alternative bubble there.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: They are very direct, if there is anything somebody doesn´t like they will let you know and if the communication is constructive, I think this is a good attribute.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1. You have more freedom on choosing the courses you like, because you can also switch courses later but at the same time this can also be quite overwhelming. 2. Everything is less structured and organized and takes more time. 3.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: It is good to start early enough with all the bureaugracy because it really takes time and there is a lot of paperwork to be done. Also checking out in advance how the semesters, exam periods and deadlines are organized might help.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: During summer spending time at the Danube was the biggest highlight! It is so green along the river, the water temperature is perfect and it is always possible to also find a quiet spot where it is less bussy.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: During winter people spent most of their time inside which is fine but it is therefore also important to have nice and cozy place to feel good during the gray and rainy days and to have good company.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
